units.title: Tema 1: I cambiamenti della società italiana

outcomes.text: Describe changing attitudes to marriage, couples and the family in Italy.
Discuss the phenomenon of the mammoni, adults living with their parents.
Describe the Italian school system and students' problems.
Discuss the brain drain (la fuga dei cervelli).
Discuss gender equality at work.
Explain unemployment and family businesses.
Describe new working patterns.

units.title: Tema 2: La cultura politica ed artistica nei Paesi di lingua italiana

outcomes.text: Describe changes and developments in music.
Explain the impact of music on popular culture.
Discuss freedom of expression.
Compare print and online press.
Explain the media's impact on society and politics.
Describe festivals, customs and traditions in Italian-speaking communities.

units.title: Tema 3: L'Italia: una società in evoluzione

outcomes.text: Explain the contribution of immigrants and migrants to Italy's economy and culture.

topics.title: I problemi della migrazione in Italia

outcomes.text: Describe marginalisation and alienation of migrants.
Discuss integration.
Explain the impact of emigration.
Describe movements between North and South.
Explain the role of Italian industries.
Describe socio-cultural differences.
Discuss the effects of organised crime.

units.title: Tema 4: Dal fascismo ai giorni nostri

outcomes.text: Explain the birth of the Fascist Party and Mussolini's rise to power.

topics.title: Il Fascismo durante la Seconda Guerra Mondiale

subtopics.title: Fascism in the Second World War

outcomes.text: Describe Mussolini's government and dictatorship.
Describe life under Mussolini during the Second World War.
Explain the fall of Mussolini and the liberation.
Describe Italy's path from dictatorship to democracy.

topics.title: Paper 1 skills: listening, reading and translation

outcomes.text: Understand main points, gist and detail of spoken Italian across registers, including online media.
Summarise spoken sources and report key points.
Understand factual and abstract authentic texts, including contemporary, historical and literary ones.
Infer meaning from complex written material.
Translate an unseen Italian passage on one of the four themes into English.

topics.title: Paper 2 skills: response to works and translation

outcomes.text: Translate an unseen English passage on one of the themes into Italian.

subtopics.title: Writing about literary texts and films

outcomes.text: Write critical and analytical essays in Italian on form, technique, key concepts, issues and social context.
Present viewpoints, develop arguments and evaluate with evidence from the work.
Study the novel Il giorno della civetta by Leonardo Sciascia (1961).
Study the novel Io non ho paura by Niccolò Ammaniti (2001).
Study the novel Jack Frusciante è uscito dal gruppo by Enrico Brizzi (1994).
Study the novel Lessico famigliare by Natalia Ginzburg (1963).
Study the short stories Marcovaldo by Italo Calvino (1963).
Study the novel Senza sangue by Alessandro Baricco (2002).
Study the novel Volevo i pantaloni by Lara Cardella (1989).
Study the play Sei personaggi in cerca d'autore by Luigi Pirandello (1921).
Study the films I cento passi (2000) and Il Postino (1994).
Study the films La grande bellezza (2013) and La vita è bella (1997).
Study the films Nuovo cinema paradiso (1988) and Va' dove ti porta il cuore (1996).
Discuss one theme from a stimulus of two statements, using a range of accurate language.
Carry out independent research on a theme or interest related to Italian-speaking society.
Summarise at least two written sources and give a personal response.
Answer questions and discuss the research.
Use gender, plurals, and definite, indefinite and partitive articles with prepositions.
Use agreement, position, apocopation, comparatives, superlatives and demonstrative, indefinite, possessive and interrogative adjectives.
Use cardinal and ordinal numerals and express time and date.
Form adverbs in -mente and use quantifiers and interrogative adverbs.
Use subject, object, disjunctive, reflexive, relative, demonstrative, indefinite, possessive and interrogative pronouns, with ci and ne.
Use simple and complex prepositions and coordinating and subordinating conjunctions.
Conjugate regular, modal, irregular and reflexive verbs and use impersonal and negative forms.
Use present, perfect, imperfect, future, conditional, pluperfect and (receptively) past historic tenses.
Use the passive, continuous tenses with stare, gerund and participles.
Use the subjunctive in present, perfect, imperfect and pluperfect forms, including hypothetical clauses with se.
Handle negation, questions, commands, word order inversion and time expressions with da and fa.
